description_full: The RMR Group Inc., through its subsidiary, provides real estate asset management services in the United States. The company offers management services to publicly traded equity real estate investment trusts; diversified healthcare trust, which owns senior living communities, medical office and life science properties and other healthcare related properties; industrial logistics properties trusts that owns and leases industrial and logistics properties; office properties income trust which owns and leases office properties primarily to single tenants and those with high credit quality characteristics; and service properties trust. It also provides advisory services to publicly traded mortgage real estate investment trust. In addition, the company provides management services to franchisor and operator of hotels, resorts and cruise ships; private funds, joint ventures and the underlying residential real estate assets of the funds, as well as property management services to third party owners; and private capital vehicles, including ABP trust and other private entities that own commercial real estate. The company was formerly known as REIT Management & Research Inc. and changed its name to The RMR Group Inc. in October 2015. The RMR Group Inc. was founded in 1986 and is headquartered in Newton, Massachusetts.
ceo_bio: Mr. Adam David Portnoy | CEO, President, MD & Chairman | Age 55 | Compensation: $2.7M (FY2025)
culture_narrative: Employs approximately 800 people. Revenue per employee of $804K ranks in the below the sector median among Real Estate peers, with revenue growing 9%/yr across its filed history. Each employee generates $81K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $20K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 3× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags moderate compensation governance risk (6/10).
financial_summary: The RMR Group Inc. is a micro-cap real estate business with a $283M market cap on $643M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at -13% over the past three years and +9% annually across the full decade, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome. Operating margins are contracting by -4.9pp, the first warning that competitive pressure is eroding the franchise.
Returns on capital run at 39% against a 9% cost of capital — a 30-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $65M in free cash flow — roughly 10 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 6.77× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.0× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 3.5×.

Management returns a meaningful 11.4% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 4.6% of the shares, and profit capture is only 0.3× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.

sect: Its 6% operating margin trails the Real Estate median (22%) by 16pp, so it is a below-average operator in its field.

The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 23% below the high.

The 3 covering analysts target $22.17 on average, 35% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 39% clears the cost of capital of 8.5% by 30pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.81).
It converts 10% of revenue into free cash flow.

ROE of 5% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (3.2x equity multiplier).

hlth: Leverage is conservative at 0.0x net debt to EBITDA ($51.4M of cash against $203.8M of debt), with interest covered 3.5x.
growth: Revenue has compounded at -12.6% over 3 years, 1.2% over 5 years and 9.2% over 10 years, so growth is decelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 30%).
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Free cash flow has compounded -1.7% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
Forward indicators: FFO growth of 0.2% a year over five years.
Capex runs only 0.4x depreciation (1.2% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
own: Insiders own a modest 4.6%, and institutions hold 84%.

people: With about 800 employees, each generates about $804K of revenue, 0.4x the Real Estate median, and revenue has grown 9.2% a year across its filed history.
